claims.text: Mild thermal annealing relieves residual strain and interfacial stress in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films or nanoribbons.
Relieving residual strain and interfacial stress improves local structural ordering at grain boundaries and interfaces.
Improved local ordering produces a more uniform magnetic microstructure and more uniform domain coupling.
The more uniform magnetic microstructure permits more cooperative magnetic-domain switching.
Annealing-induced structural and magnetic uniformity sharpens the magnetic transition.
Annealing-induced ordering lowers the energy barriers for domain-wall motion.
Annealing will increase the magnetic entropy change relative to the as-deposited baseline under low applied fields.
A higher magnetic entropy-change magnitude represents an enhanced magnetocaloric response.
Annealing will narrow the hysteresis loop and lower coercivity relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Hysteretic losses can be important for magnetocaloric refrigeration performance.
Improved structural uniformity may improve local heat transfer and modestly increase cycle frequency.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons possess significant residual strain, interfacial stress, and local disorder.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons have a broadened magnetic transition and significant hysteresis.
Residual strain, interfacial stress, and local disorder limit the baseline magnetocaloric response.
Annealing at approximately 300–400 °C under an inert atmosphere can relieve stress without causing phase segregation or excessive grain growth if appropriately timed.
The proposed mechanism applies under low magnetic fields near the alloy's magnetic transition temperature in nanoscale thin films or nanoribbons.
Heat-transfer rates limit the attainable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency in the nanoscale geometries considered.
The magnitude of magnetocaloric enhancement and hysteresis reduction depends on annealing conditions and the initial disorder level.
Failure to observe both the predicted magnetic-performance changes and the proposed structural mediator relative to an as-deposited control would falsify the hypothesis.
